extracted.intended_audience: Guardian News & Media editorial staff and freelance contributors
extracted.subtask_description: Editorial and ethical guidelines for journalists working for Guardian News & Media (GNM), covering professional practice, personal behaviour, conflicts of interest and the PCC Code of Practice. Intended to protect trust, integrity and legal compliance in print and online journalism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attribution — anonymous quotations
rubrics_metrics.description: We recognise that people will often speak more honestly if they are allowed to speak anonymously. The use of non-attributed quotes can therefore often assist the reader towards a truer understanding of a subject than if a journalist confined him/herself to quoting bland on-the-record quotes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be honest about sources even if you can't name them. Anonymous pejorative quotes are rarely acceptable: paraphrase them unless there are exceptional circumstances and consultation with the senior editor of the day. The New York Times policy on pejorative quotes is noted: vivid language confers an unfair advantage on a speaker who hides behind the newspaper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attribution — anonymous contributions
rubrics_metrics.description: Articles commissioned by GNM should be published anonymously or pseudonymously only in exceptional circumstances, for example where the author's safety, privacy or livelihood may be compromised, and only with the permission of the relevant editor or managing editor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Readers should be made aware that identities have been obscured or withheld. This provision need not apply to user-generated content or established pseudonymous authors commissioned in that capacity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Credits and bylines
rubrics_metrics.description: Staff must not reproduce other people’s material without attribution, other than in exceptional circumstances, and only with permission of the most senior editor on duty. Bylines should be carried only on material that is substantially the work of the bylined journalist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledge sources of published material obtained from another organisation, including quotes taken from other newspaper articles. If an article contains a significant amount of agency copy the agency should be credited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bribery and facilitation payments
rubrics_metrics.description: The Bribery Act 2010 creates offences including offering or accepting advantages to improperly perform an activity and bribing foreign public officials; facilitation payments to public officials abroad can fall within the Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Staff should discuss with their managing editor beforehand if concerned that any payments might fall into these categories. If such payments are requested or made, inform the editor-in-chief or managing editor as soon as possible. There is no public interest defence except possible duress in life-or-limb situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Children — special care
rubrics_metrics.description: Special care should be taken when dealing with children (under the age of 16). Heads of departments must be informed when children have been photographed or interviewed without parental consent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intrusions into children's private lives need a strong public interest justification. Consider obscuring identities because of the longevity of online material. If a journalist considers making their own child the subject of an article, seek consent where the child is reasonably able to make an informed decision. See PCC code section 6.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commissioning practice
rubrics_metrics.description: GNM supports good commissioning practice, including fair treatment of freelances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors should reference GNM’s Freelance Charter when commissioning new contributors and ensure freelances are aware of rules such as declarations of interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copy approval
rubrics_metrics.description: The general rule is that no one should be given the right to copy approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In certain circumstances people may be shown copy or quotes but the paper is not required to alter copy. Avoid offering copy approval as a method of securing interviews or co-operation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyright and rights clearance
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists should not use content from non-authorised third-party sources—pictures, text or other media—without obtaining necessary permissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There are limited legal situations where permission may not be needed but check with the picture desk or editorial legal before using without permission. Familiarise with internal guidelines on rights and use of content from public websites.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct quotations must not be altered
rubrics_metrics.description: Direct quotations should not be changed to alter their context or meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Endorsements
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists should not agree to promote through copy, photographs or footnotes the financial interests of prospective interviewees or contributors, or their sponsors, as a means of securing access to them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Promotional information should be included only where, in the editor's judgment, it is of genuine interest or assistance to the reader.

rubrics_metrics.name: Errors and corrections
rubrics_metrics.description: It is the policy of the GNM to correct significant errors as soon as possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journalists must cooperate frankly with readers’ editors and report errors to them. All complaints should be brought to readers' editors. Journalists should read corrections columns regularly.

rubrics_metrics.name: External assistance
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists should not engage the paid services of external non-journalistic agents or assistants without prior knowledge and approval of the editor-in-chief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fairness
rubrics_metrics.description: The voice of opponents no less than of friends has a right to be heard; the more serious the criticism or allegations the greater the obligation to allow the subject the opportunity to respond.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grief — sensitivity
rubrics_metrics.description: People should be treated with sensitivity during periods of grief and trauma.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See PCC code section 5. Handle approaches and publication sensitively when reporting on individuals in grief or shock.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language and use of swear words
rubrics_metrics.description: Respect for the reader demands that words likely to offend should not be used casually. Use swear words only when absolutely necessary to the facts or to portray a character.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid placing swear words in headlines, pull quotes and standfirsts; never use asterisks to mask them. The stronger the word, the stronger the justification needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal — libel and contempt
rubrics_metrics.description: Our libel and contempt laws are complex; staff should familiarise themselves with the current state of the law and seek training if unconfident.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult in-house legal or night lawyers on specific concerns and read legal bulletins emailed by legal. Report PCC and libel judgments promptly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment policy
rubrics_metrics.description: In general, GNM does not pay for stories, except from bona fide freelance sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rare exceptions must be approved by the editor or his deputies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Photographs — digital alteration
rubrics_metrics.description: Digitally enhanced or altered images, montages and illustrations should be clearly labeled as such.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privacy — proportionality and Omand principles
rubrics_metrics.description: Respect people's privacy; avoid invading privacy unless there is a clear public interest. Proportionality is essential and prior consideration must be given where privacy issues may be involved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply five adapted Omand questions before intruding: (1) sufficient cause justified by scale of potential harm; (2) integrity of motive—public good from publication; (3) proportionate methods using minimum intrusion; (4) proper authority and senior-level approval; (5) reasonable prospect of success—avoid 'fishing' expeditions. Exercise caution about publishing identifying details that enable further intrusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Race, ethnicity and religion
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not publish someone’s race, ethnic background or religion unless that information is pertinent to the story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not report race of criminal suspects unless part of a description to identify them or relevant to the story (e.g., hate crime).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sources — confidentiality and identification
rubrics_metrics.description: Sources promised confidentiality must be protected at all costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where possible, identify sources as specifically as possible. Responsibility for satisfaction with sources rests with desk editors as well as reporters; sub-editors should challenge dependability of information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subterfuge and identification
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists should generally identify themselves as GNM employees when working on a story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions for stories of exceptional public interest require approval of a head of department. This applies to anything published, including information obtained by others' subterfuge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suicide reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Exercise particular care in reporting suicide or issues involving suicide, bearing in mind the risk of encouraging others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be careful in presentation, use of pictures and describing methods. Refer to substances in general terms where possible and consider relatives' feelings. When appropriate, include helpline numbers (Samaritans UK 116 123; US Lifeline 1-800-273-8255; Australia Lifeline 13 11 14).

rubrics_metrics.name: Verification
rubrics_metrics.description: Trust in the authenticity and reliability of sources is essential. Skepticism should be the starting point for web and email sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be tenacious in seeking reliable corroboration and state the level of substantiation achieved (e.g., 'the Guardian has been unable independently to verify the facts'). Do not state as fact information from someone who cannot be authenticated; explain interview medium when relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflicts of interest — general
rubrics_metrics.description: Staff should be sensitive to possible conflicts between outside activities (organisations, companies, political parties) and the integrity of our journalism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be transparent about outside personal, philosophical or financial interests that might conflict or be perceived to conflict with professional performance. If in doubt consult a head of department, managing/deputy editors or the editor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declarations of interest (when writing about connected matters)
rubrics_metrics.description: It is always necessary to declare an interest when the journalist is writing about something with which he or she has a significant connection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Declare to a head of department or editor during preparation; full transparency may require a declaration in print and online. A connection need not be formal (e.g., acting in an advisory capacity). Obvious connections that are the reason for contribution should be stated at end of the contribution. Generally do not write about or quote a relative/partner; if exception, make the connection clear. Commissioning editors must ensure freelances are aware.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declarations of corporate interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognise and acknowledge that Guardian and Observer are part of a wider group of media companies; be careful to acknowledge those relationships in stories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anyone writing about GMG-related businesses should seek comments and/or confirmation in the normal way. Staff should familiarise themselves with GMG companies and interests; summary provided in appendix.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial reporting — share register and restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Business desk maintains a register of personal shares; all staff are expected to list shares, transactions and investments that ought to be disclosed because of potential conflicts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Financial journalists may own shares but should not be market traders regularly. The Code prohibits using financial information for personal profit; restricts writing about shares where a journalist or close family has significant interest without internal disclosure; forbids dealing in shares about which they have written recently or intend to write; requires care to distinguish comment/conjecture/fact, especially when making investment recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Freelance work
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid freelance writing for house magazines of particular businesses or causes if the contribution could be interpreted as an endorsement of the concern.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If in doubt consult your head of department.

rubrics_metrics.name: Freebies, gifts and hospitality
rubrics_metrics.description: Staff should not use their position to obtain private benefit for themselves or others; GNM will not allow payment, gift or other advantage to undermine accuracy, fairness or independence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report any attempts to induce favourable editorial treatment. Disclose relevant payments/gifts. Make clear when travel/accommodation costs have been borne by an airline, hotel or other interest. Acceptance conditional on GNM's editorial freedom. Partners/family should not usually be included in free arrangements; additional costs should be paid by the journalist. Gifts under £50 are acceptable; gifts over £50 should be returned or entered into an annual charity raffle. Staff must not be influenced by commercial considerations including advertisers.

rubrics_metrics.name: GNM connections — using position
rubrics_metrics.description: Staff members should not use their positions to seek any benefit or advantage in personal business, financial or commercial transactions not afforded to the public generally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use company stationery or cite connection to resolve consumer grievances, get quicker service or seek discounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interaction with readers
rubrics_metrics.description: Courtesy applies whether an exchange takes place in person, by telephone, letter or email.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be mindful of internal blogging and social media guidelines; online exchanges can be more informal or combative but journalists must follow guidance available on internal Really Social Media site.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outside engagements or duties — notification and restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Staff should inform their immediate editor if they intend to give evidence to court; chair public forums/seminars arranged by commercial organisers; undertake outside employment likely to conflict; chair public or political forums or appear on platforms; make representations or give evidence to official bodies in connection with GNM-published material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journalists invited to chair debates or appear on panels as a representative of GNM should not usually accept payment unless significant private time is required; acceptance of payment must be approved in advance by the managing editor. Travel and reasonable expenses may be accepted. Generally do not provide PR advice to paid audiences; consult managing editor if in doubt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relationships — reporting on relatives or close associates
rubrics_metrics.description: Staff members should not write about, photograph or make news judgments about any individual related by blood or marriage or with whom the staff member has a close personal, financial or romantic relationship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If placed in circumstances with potential for this kind of conflict, advise the department head.

rubrics_metrics.name: PCC Code — Accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: The Press must take care not to publish inaccurate, misleading or distorted information, including pictures. A significant inaccuracy must be corrected promptly with due prominence. Distinguish clearly between comment, conjecture and fact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report fairly and accurately outcomes of defamation actions involving the publication unless settlement states otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: PCC Code — Opportunity to reply
rubrics_metrics.description: A fair opportunity for reply to inaccuracies must be given when reasonably called for.

rubrics_metrics.name: PCC Code — Privacy
rubrics_metrics.description: Everyone is entitled to respect for private and family life, home, health and correspondence, including digital communications. Editors must justify intrusions into private life without consent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Account will be taken of complainant's own public disclosures. It is unacceptable to photograph individuals in private places without consent. Note: private places are those where a reasonable expectation of privacy exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: PCC Code — Harassment
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists must not engage in intimidation, harassment or persistent pursuit; must not persist in questioning, telephoning, pursuing or photographing individuals once asked to desist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If requested, identify yourself and whom you represent. Editors must ensure these principles are observed by those working for them and avoid using non-compliant material from other sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: PCC Code — Intrusion into grief or shock
rubrics_metrics.description: In cases involving personal grief or shock, enquiries and approaches must be made with sympathy and discretion and publication handled sensitively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This should not restrict right to report legal proceedings, such as inquests. When reporting suicide, avoid excessive detail about method.

rubrics_metrics.name: PCC Code — Children (general provisions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Young people should be free to complete their time at school without unnecessary intrusion. A child under 16 must not be interviewed or photographed on issues involving their own or another child's welfare unless a custodial parent or responsible adult consents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pupils must not be approached or photographed at school without permission of school authorities. Minors must not be paid for material involving children's welfare unless clearly in child's interest. Do not publish details of a child's private life based solely on fame of a parent/guardian.

rubrics_metrics.name: PCC Code — Children in sex cases
rubrics_metrics.description: The press must not identify children under 16 who are victims or witnesses in sex offence cases. In any report: the child must not be identified; the adult may be; the word 'incest' must not be used where a child victim might be identified; care must be taken that nothing implies relationship between accused and child.

rubrics_metrics.name: PCC Code — Hospitals
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists must identify themselves and obtain permission from a responsible executive before entering non-public areas of hospitals to pursue enquiries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Restrictions on intruding into privacy are particularly relevant to enquiries about individuals in hospitals or similar institutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: PCC Code — Reporting of crime
rubrics_metrics.description: Relatives or friends of persons convicted or accused of crime should not generally be identified without their consent unless genuinely relevant. Pay particular regard to potentially vulnerable children who witness or are victims of crime.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This should not restrict reporting legal proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: PCC Code — Clandestine devices and subterfuge
rubrics_metrics.description: The press must not seek to obtain or publish material acquired by hidden cameras, clandestine listening devices, intercepting private communications, unauthorised removal of documents/photos, or accessing digitally-held private information without consent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Misrepresentation or subterfuge can only generally be justified in the public interest and only when the material cannot be obtained by other means.

rubrics_metrics.name: PCC Code — Victims of sexual assault
rubrics_metrics.description: The press must not identify victims of sexual assault or publish material likely to contribute to such identification unless there is adequate justification and they are legally free to do so.

rubrics_metrics.name: PCC Code — Discrimination
rubrics_metrics.description: The press must avoid prejudicial or pejorative reference to an individual's race, colour, religion, gender, sexual orientation or to any physical or mental illness or disability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Details of such characteristics must be avoided unless genuinely relevant to the story.

rubrics_metrics.name: PCC Code — Financial journalism
rubrics_metrics.description: Even where law does not prohibit it, journalists must not use for their own profit financial information received in advance of general publication, nor pass such information to others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose significant personal financial interests to editor; do not buy/sell shares about which they have written recently or intend to write; distinguish between comment/conjecture/fact when making investment recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: PCC Code — Confidential sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists have a moral obligation to protect confidential sources of information.

rubrics_metrics.name: PCC Code — Witness payments in criminal trials
rubrics_metrics.description: No payment or offer of payment to a witness or person who may be called as a witness should be made in any case once proceedings are active as defined by Contempt of Court Act 1981; prohibition lasts until suspect is freed unconditionally or proceedings discontinue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where proceedings are not yet active but likely, editors must not make/offer payment unless demonstrably in public interest and all steps taken to ensure no financial dealings influence evidence. Any payment made to a person later cited to give evidence must be disclosed to prosecution and defence and the witness advised.

rubrics_metrics.name: PCC Code — Payment to criminals
rubrics_metrics.description: Payment or offers for stories/pictures/information that seek to exploit a crime or glorify crime must not be made directly or via agents to convicted/confessed criminals or associates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors invoking public interest to justify payment must demonstrate good reason; if no public interest emerges, material should not be published.

rubrics_metrics.name: PCC Code — The public interest (tests and examples)
rubrics_metrics.description: Exceptions to clauses marked * may be demonstrated to be in the public interest. Public interest includes detecting/exposing crime or serious impropriety; protecting public health and safety; preventing the public from being misled by actions/statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public interest also includes freedom of expression. Editors must demonstrate they reasonably believed publication/activity would be in the public interest and will consider whether material is already in the public domain. Exceptional public interest needed to override normally paramount interest of children under 16.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appendix — Areas of interest and companies held by GMG (disclosure of corporate holdings)
rubrics_metrics.description: Summary of GMG's portfolio and areas of interest, including wholly owned businesses (GNM, GMG Radio, GMG Property Services), joint ventures (Trader Media Group, Emap) and other investments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Staff should familiarise themselves with these holdings and disclose/acknowledge connections when relevant to stories.
